title: First Practical Experiences Integrating Quantum Computers with HPC Resources: A Case Study With a 20-qubit Superconducting Quantum Computer
problem: Integrating quantum computers with traditional HPC systems presents facility, operational, and training challenges
motivation: Quantum computing requires specialized facility management; practical integration roadmap needed for HPC centers
method: The researchers connected a real 20-qubit superconducting quantum computer (where quantum bits are stored in circuits cooled to near absolute zero) with a traditional supercomputer at Germany's Leibniz Supercomputing Centre. Rather than simulate or theorize, they documented what actually had to work: power delivery and cooling systems, software connections between the quantum and classical computers, and operator training. This hands-on integration revealed practical challenges that isolated lab experiments don't show.
key_novelty: This work shows what actually must happen in practice when combining a quantum computer and a supercomputer in a real computing facility.
contributions: Facility requirements survey for quantum computer deployment in HPC
Automated quantum recalibration within HPC scheduler
